title: Research: the 916 open mixed GL3 target pairs need exactly their direct cost (no new kappa)
body:
## Contribution

This closes open question 1 of `research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-seed18/` (Hanson Sun, on main). The model is the same: M_2(F2[GL_3(F2)]) with 36 paid involutions `I + N([g]+[e])`, where g is one of six coordinate CNOTs and N one of six binary rank-one idempotents. Free GL_2(F2) scalar mixing is allowed, and the target `diag([a],[b])` must hold with formal equality. Seed18 left 916 ordered pairs with direct cost 10..12 at "minimum >= 9". **Each of them needs exactly its direct cost d(a)+d(b):**

| direct cost | pairs | exact minimum | new exclusion |
|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 10 | 816 | 10 | no length-9 word |
| 11 | 96 | 11 | no word of length 9 or 10 |
| 12 | 4 | 12 | no word of length 9, 10 or 11 |

With seed18's table, all 28,224 ordered pairs cost exactly d(a)+d(b). Heterogeneous targets never share paid work in this alphabet. The four cost-12 pairs use the two 3-cycle permutation matrices, which are the only elements at distance 6.

**Bounded third-register probe.** `engine3.cpp` adds one extra dirty scalar register, which must be restored or may end at any monomial `[c]`. That gives 28 idempotents x 6 labels = 168 paid involutions. A radius-3 ball (2,705,791 states) plus 450,868,320 streamed distance-4 images covers every word of length at most 7. **No pair gets a word shorter than d(a)+d(b).** All direct words of length at most 7 are found as positive controls. So the extra register saves nothing for the 24,224 pairs with direct cost at most 8, and pairs with direct cost at least 9 still need at least 8 calls. Lengths 8 and above with a third register are not covered.

## Method and evidence

- `engine.cpp` is a new C++17 engine that shares no code with seed18. It builds the exact radius-4 ball and streams the distance-5 layer. It reuses seed18's row-orbit lemma: `A B^-1 = diag([a],[b])` exactly when each row of A is a left translate of the same row of B. It groups the 16,292,362 radius-5 states by canonical row keys, compared exactly with no digests. The join covers 1,119,282,418 ordered pairs, which is every word of length at most 10.
- **Length-11 stage, for the four cost-12 pairs only.** It streams all 562,639,176 images `hC`, with C at distance 5, and looks each one up exactly among the radius-5 groups.
- **Reproduces seed18.** The radius-4 layers 1/36/996/25,518/636,945, the 133,207 cosets and the table `min(9, d(a)+d(b))` all match at every pair.
- **Positive controls on the same code paths.** For the 27,308 pairs with direct cost at most 9, the radius-5 join returns exactly the direct cost. It finds a length-10 word for every cost-10 pair. The length-11 stage, run on all 96 cost-11 pairs, finds an 11-call word for each one.
- **`verify.py` is stdlib.** It has its own formal algebra. It re-derives the 916 pairs and checks all 816 + 96 recorded words and the four direct twelve-call words formally. It binds the receipt to seed18's pinned certificate and rejects tampered witnesses. Five tampered `RESULT.json` variants were also rejected by hand. `--full` compiles the engine with `-Wall -Wextra -Werror`, reruns it and requires the parsed output to equal `RESULT.json`.

## Reproduction

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10/verify.py          # quick, < 1 s
python3 -I -B research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10/verify.py --full   # C++17, ~3 GB RAM, 65-120 s
python3 -I -B research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10/verify.py --three  # third-register probe, ~35 s, 2.3 GB
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/bit-gl3-mixed-targets-length10 --check-only
```

One read-only OpenAI Codex review of the two-register part found no must-fix issues. It confirmed the coverage cases, the key, anchor and dedupe exactness, the length-11 binary search and the absence of data races. Its two should-fixes are applied: quick mode now pins the complete engine receipt and histogram and rejects duplicate rows, and the README wording on length-11 hits is corrected. The third-register probe was added after that review and was not part of it. Quick mode passes on CPython 3.10–3.14 and in the registered 3.12 replay (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=negative-result`). `--full --three` passes on macOS with Apple clang in 114 s on 10 cores. Runs with 4 and 10 threads give identical receipts and tables. `--check-only` passes.

## Limits

- This is a finite certificate for exactly two scalar registers, this alphabet and these targets.
- It covers no extra or dirty registers, other labels, physical, compiler, hosting or precision admission, or transfer to the rational-frame supplier. No kappa or selected-record change is claimed.
- The lower bounds rest on one engine. Seed18's independent replay corroborates only the radius-4 part.
- No dedicated CI workflow is added, and the registered quick command does not compile C++.
- Seed18's README still says these minima are unresolved. It is a frozen predecessor, so it is left unchanged.

## Open next questions

The package README lists three: a dirty third register at length 8 or more, a written invariant for `min = d(a)+d(b)`, and a second independent radius-5 join.

## Credit and overlap

- Model, coverage lemma, radius-4 table and the question: Hanson Sun's seed18 package, with its retained lineage (eumemic PR288, Ali Romman PR468, Gareth Davidson PR1333).
- PR1804 (1337isnot1337, head `26f5ae8a`) treats one cost-6 pair, which is already inside seed18's exact table.
- PR1696 (same author, head `4dadd274`) studies heterogeneous GL2 targets, a different group.
- The overlap check was refreshed at 2026-10-14 15:38Z (540 open PRs, 602 discussions) and found nothing on the 916 pairs. That is not a novelty certificate.
- Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-18927159
